title: Certificates of Deposit: The Relationship Bonus and Pricing of a Renewed Term
content:
Customers who bank with Piedmont Crescent Bank through a qualifying Personal Checking account earn extra points on their Certificates of Deposit. This page explains that Relationship Bonus, and how the rate of a renewed term is priced.

## The Relationship Bonus

A term earns the Relationship Bonus when the customer holds, on the date that counts (the opening date for a new certificate, the renewal date for a renewed term), a checking account in active status whose tier is on the qualifying list of the certificate's tier. The bonus adds the tier's Relationship Bonus points to both the interest rate and the APY of that term.

| Tier | Relationship Bonus points | Checking tiers that qualify | Bonus re-tested at each renewal | Renewal priced on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 0.10 | Interest Checking, Premier Checking, Private Client Checking | Yes | figures published on the maturity date |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 0.05 | Premier Checking, Private Client Checking | Yes | figures published on the maturity date |
| 12-Month Certificate | 0.15 | Interest Checking, Premier Checking, Private Client Checking | Yes | figures published on the maturity date |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 0.15 | Interest Checking, Premier Checking, Private Client Checking | Yes | figures published on the maturity date |
| 36-Month Certificate | 0.20 | Interest Checking, Premier Checking, Private Client Checking | Yes | figures published on the maturity date |
| 60-Month Certificate | 0.20 | Interest Checking, Premier Checking, Private Client Checking | Yes | figures published on the maturity date |

## Pricing a renewed term

A renewed term is priced from the published standard interest rate and standard APY of the tier it renews into, as those figures stand on the maturity date, plus the bonus points the new term earns. Because every tier re-tests its bonuses at renewal, both the Jumbo Bonus and the Relationship Bonus are judged afresh on the renewal date; a bonus held in the old term carries over only if it is earned again.

## Bonuses do not change mid-term

- A bonus the term earned at its start stays in the rate until that term ends, even if its basis disappears later, for instance because the qualifying checking account is closed.
- A bonus that becomes available during a term, for instance because a qualifying checking account is opened, is not added to the running term; it can first count at the start of the next term.

## Truth table (hypothetical holdings on the date that counts)

| Certificate tier | Checking held on that date | Relationship Bonus earned? |
|---|---|---|
| 12-Month Certificate | Interest Checking, active | Yes |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | Interest Checking, active | No, Interest Checking is not on this tier's list |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | Premier Checking, active | Yes |
| 36-Month Certificate | Private Client Checking, opened the day after the date that counts | No for this term |
| 60-Month Certificate | Premier Checking, active on the date that counts, closed in month four | Yes, and it stays for the whole term |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A 36-Month Certificate renews into its own tier. On the maturity date the published figures for that tier happen to be different from those at the certificate's opening; the new term takes the figures published on the maturity date. If the owner holds an active Premier Checking account on the renewal date, 0.20 points are added to that published rate and to that published APY.
